svg.title: The condition determines the denominator in the same two-way count table
svg.desc: A student is chosen uniformly from all sixty students. A means club member and B means travels by bus. Rows A and A prime have counts twelve, eighteen and twenty-four, six in columns B and B prime. Row totals are thirty and thirty; column totals thirty-six and twenty-four; grand total sixty. The left copy highlights the bus-traveller column, with twelve club members among thirty-six bus travellers, so probability of A given B is twelve over thirty-six, one third. The right copy highlights the club-member row, with twelve bus travellers among thirty club members, so probability of B given A is twelve over thirty, two fifths. Both use the same intersection numerator but different conditioning totals. The joint probability uses the grand total, twelve over sixty, one fifth. All conditioning groups in this example have positive size.
